questions.q: What ingestion pattern does this capstone use to move Northfield's data into S3?
options: A nightly bcp export from SQL Server, uploaded via the AWS CLI to a date-partitioned S3 key
Real-time change data capture streamed continuously via Kinesis
Manual drag-and-drop uploads through the S3 console each morning
A direct database link between SQL Server and Redshift, bypassing S3 entirely
questions.explain: The lesson uses a scheduled nightly bcp export uploaded with the AWS CLI, matching Northfield's actual same-day (not real-time) requirement.

questions.q: Why is a nightly scheduled export the right choice for Northfield instead of AWS DMS with change data capture?
options: Leadership asked for same-day visibility, not real-time updates, so a nightly batch matches the actual requirement
DMS cannot connect to SQL Server under any circumstances
Nightly exports are always technically superior to CDC
AWS does not support CDC for on-premises databases
questions.explain: The guide is explicit: same-day visibility doesn't require real-time CDC, so the right-sized tool is a scheduled export, with DMS named as the scale-up path if requirements change.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the empty _SUCCESS marker file written after each night's upload?
options: It signals to Step Functions that both files uploaded cleanly, so a partial upload never triggers a downstream run
It stores a checksum of the uploaded files for data validation
It is required by S3 for every object upload
It triggers the Glue ETL job directly, bypassing the crawler
questions.explain: The _SUCCESS marker is a completion signal Step Functions checks for before starting the crawler, preventing runs against incomplete data.

questions.q: What does the --sse AES256 flag do on the S3 upload commands in this lesson?
options: Enables server-side encryption at rest for the uploaded object
Compresses the file before upload
Splits the upload into multiple parts for speed
Sets the S3 storage class to Glacier
questions.explain: --sse AES256 turns on server-side encryption so every object in the raw zone is encrypted at rest by default.

questions.q: What is the key naming pattern used for the nightly order export?
options: s3://northfield-raw-zone/orders/dt=2026-09-19/orders_2026-09-19.csv
s3://northfield-raw-zone/2026-09-19-orders.csv
s3://northfield-orders/latest.csv
s3://northfield-raw-zone/orders.csv (overwritten nightly)
questions.explain: The key uses the orders/ prefix with a Hive-style dt=2026-09-19 partition, matching the layout decided in Lesson 2's architecture plan.
